research_rationale:
Executive Order 12830 (58 FR 4061, January 13, 1993) establishes the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal. The held Federal Register text was read in full; the four sections are separate commands with no end date, condition or sunset. The only held later instrument is Executive Order 13286 section 28, which substituted the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Secretary of Transportation in Sections 1 and 4. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) still prints the order as amended. The three bounded searches found no revocation, supersession or expiry. The order is therefore claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. The original is the Federal Register text layer; its page images were not separately re-read.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12879 (58 FR 59929, November 10, 1993) fixes the order of succession to act as Secretary of the Navy. The held Federal Register text was read in full (it is OCR text with spaced-out headings; the substance is legible). Section 1 lists four successors and rules on temporary absences, precedence and acting officers; Section 2 makes succession temporary. The order has no end date. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it. Four notes in the U.S. Code (10 U.S.C. 8013, 8015, 8017 and 5 U.S.C. 3345) still point to it as the governing order of succession. The order is therefore claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. Whether statutes such as the Vacancies Act now govern in parallel is outside the held evidence; the notes show the Code treats the order as continuing.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12938 (59 FR 59099, November 16, 1994) declares a national emergency about the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery, directs export controls, sanctions on foreign persons (Section 4) and on foreign countries (Section 5), and implementation by the Secretaries of State, the Treasury and Commerce. Executive Order 13094 (1998) revised Section 4 and a cross-reference in Section 6, Executive Order 13128 (1999) added subsection 3(e), and Executive Order 13382 (2005) revised Section 4(a); under the strike-and-restate ruling the amended clauses continue. Twenty-nine annual continuation notices are held, the last dated November 5, 2025, which continues the emergency beyond November 14, 2025 and so covers 2026-10-14 (the 2009 notice is not held). The eCFR (amended through 2026-11-06) still carries the Weapons of Mass Destruction Trade Control Regulations citing the order as amended. The inventory was corrected to add the opening declaration of emergency. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end. The held amendments are Executive Order 13094 (revision of section 4 and a cross-reference in section 6), Executive Order 13128 (new subsection 3(e)) and Executive Order 13382 (revision of section 4(a)); the Office of the Federal Register notes record these as amendments and no revocation. The other held actor texts recite the order or rely on its emergency.
Current basis: Current predicate: the part 539 regulations (31 CFR 539.106 and 539.301 and the authority line, eCFR amended through 2026-11-06) still cite the order as amended by Executive Orders 13094 and 13382, and the nonproliferation statute note to 50 U.S.C. 1701 refers to subsections 4(b) and (c); the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no instrument ending any clause.
savings_reason: No clause has ended; the bounded searches found only amendments and the yearly continuation notices.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end. The Office of the Federal Register amendment notes (Executive Orders 13094, 13128, 13382) were reconciled by citing each as a later event on the clauses it changes (Sections 3, 4 and 6); none revokes any clause. Section 4 and the Section 6 cross-reference were restated or amended, so under the strike-and-restate ruling they continue, amended, with the before and after text recorded.
scope_check: The inventory was corrected to add the declaration of national emergency (the machine inventory began at the order formula) and to merge the 15-character order formula into it, since a span that short cannot be verified as a quotation. Twenty-seven clauses cover the declaration (with the order formula), Sections 1 to 11 and the numbered paragraphs of Section 5(b). Subsection 3(e) and Sections 4(e) and (f) were added after the original and are not part of the original inventory.
independent_command_check: Sections 4 and 5 sanctions are separate from the export controls in Sections 2 and 3, and from the Treasury authority in Section 7. Executive Order 13382 imposes blocking sanctions under the same emergency by its own terms; those are independent commands and do not end these ones.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12957 (60 FR 14615, March 17, 1995) declares a national emergency about Iran, bars United States persons from contracts for developing or financing Iranian petroleum resources, and authorizes the Treasury to implement. Executive Order 12959 (May 6, 1995) revoked sections 1 and 2 only 'to the extent inconsistent' and says it supplements this order; Executive Order 13059 (August 19, 1997) consolidated the Iran measures but its text revokes nothing in this order. Pub. L. 109-293 section 101 (2006) provides that sanctions under sections 1 and 3 of this order as in effect on January 1, 2006 remain in effect until the President terminates them, and no termination is held. Sixteen yearly continuation notices (2011 to 2026) show the emergency continued beyond March 15, 2026, and Executive Order 14382 (February 2026) recites it. The OFAC regulations in the eCFR (amended through 2026-11-06) cite this order as authority. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. The history of notices for 1996 to 2010 is not registered in this packet.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end; its only held later instruments naming it as affected are Executive Order 12959 section 5 (conditional partial revocation of sections 1 and 2) and Executive Order 13059 (consolidating order that revokes other orders), and the yearly continuation notices keep the emergency alive.
Current basis: Current predicate: see the clause's basis. The bounded searches current-law:usc (3 hits), current-law:ecfr (13 hits, the OFAC regulations that cite this order) and later-events:ofr_catalog (26 hits: the two partial revocations, the yearly notices and later Iran orders) found no instrument ending the clause.
savings_reason: Pub. L. 109-293 section 101 keeps the sanctions under sections 1 and 3 of this order in effect by statute, independently of the order, until the President terminates them; no termination is held.

Executive Order 12959 (60 FR 24757, May 9, 1995) added trade and investment prohibitions against Iran to those in Executive Order 12957. Executive Order 13059 section 7 (August 19, 1997, effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on August 20, 1997) revoked subsections (a), (b), (c), (d) and (f) of section 1 with respect to transactions after its effective date, so those five prohibitions ended on that date. Paragraphs 1(e) (new investment) and 1(g) (evasion), the definitions, the Treasury authority in Section 3 and the remaining sections are not revoked. Pub. L. 109-293 section 101 (2006) provides that sanctions under sections 1(e), 1(g) and 3 as in effect on January 1, 2006 remain in effect until the President terminates them, and the OFAC regulations in the eCFR (amended through 2026-11-06) still cite the order. The held continuation notices run only through the March 2025 notice in this packet; the statute, not the notices, is the continuing predicate for paragraphs 1(e) and 1(g) and Section 3. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14 as to the unrevoked clauses.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end for its prohibitions; its only own-terms dates are the transition dates in Section 8(a); Executive Order 13059 section 7 revoked paragraphs 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 1(d) and 1(f) for transactions after August 20, 1997, and revoked nothing else in this order.

Executive Order 13059 (62 FR 44531, August 21, 1997) consolidates the Iran sanctions of Executive Orders 12613, 12957 and 12959: Section 1 bars imports of Iranian-origin goods, Section 2 bars exports, reexports, new investment, dealings and facilitation, Section 3 continues earlier licenses, Section 5 authorizes the Treasury, and Section 7 revokes Executive Order 12613 and parts of Executive Order 12959. The order rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12957, which the held annual notices continue through the notice of March 2, 2026. Pub. L. 109-293 section 101 (2006) keeps the sanctions under Sections 2, 3 and 5 in effect by statute, and 31 CFR part 560 still cites the order as authority. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or ends any section. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. The notices for 2015, 2016 and 2017 are not held; the later notices and the statute make the gap immaterial to the claim, and it is disclosed here.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end. The Office of the Federal Register catalog records no revocation of it; the held notes are the order's own revocations of other orders. Executive Orders 13628, 13846 and 14382 recite it among the Iran prohibitions in force and revoke none of it.

Executive Order 13106 (63 FR 68151, December 9, 1998) adjusted 1999 pay rates (Sections 1 to 6), superseded the prior pay order (Section 7) and delegated a pay administration authority by amending Executive Order 12748 (Section 8). Executive Order 13144, section 8, states that 'Sections 1 through 7 of Executive Order 13106 of December 7, 1998, are superseded', so Sections 1 to 7 ended on its date. Section 8 is not within that supersession. The U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 5301 still prints Executive Order 12748 section 2(c) with the inserted words, and the part 531 regulations still cite the order in their authority line. The order is therefore claimed as partly in force (Section 8) on 2026-10-14, with Sections 1 to 7 ended by express supersession.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: Sections 1 through 7 are ended by Executive Order 13144 section 8; Section 8 is outside that supersession and no held instrument ends it.
Current basis: Current predicate for Section 8: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 5301 prints Executive Order 12748 'as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. 13106, § 8' and shows section 2(c) with the words 'section 5304(g)–(h)' that Section 8 inserted (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09); the bounded searches current-law:usc (2 hits), current-law:ecfr (1 hit, the part 531 authority line citing this order) and later-events:ofr_catalog (2 hits, both the 13144 supersession note) found no ending of Section 8.
savings_reason: Pay rates fixed by Schedules 1 to 9 and paid for pay periods before the supersession are accrued effects of Sections 1 to 6; Executive Order 13144 replaced the schedules going forward, and the delegation in Section 8 continues in Executive Order 12748 section 2(c).
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER": "The three listed candidates are one event, the supersession of Sections 1 through 7 by Executive Order 13144 on 1999-12-21; the unnamed-actor candidate is the same supersession. It is adopted as the end of the fifteen clauses in Sections 1 to 7. Section 8, which the supersession does not name, is claimed operative, so the order stays YES."}
earlier_end_check: Sections 1 to 7 have no own-terms end earlier than the supersession; the schedules took effect on January 1, 1999 (Section 6), and Section 6 only dates their start. Executive Order 13144 is dated December 21, 1999 and its section 8 has no separate effective-date wording, so the end is recorded on its signing date; the alternative reading, that the supersession takes effect with the new schedules on January 1, 2000 (13144 section 7), is stated here for the reviewer. Section 7 of this order states a status ('is superseded') rather than an act to be performed later, so no earlier end by performance is shown. The Office of the Federal Register note 'Superseded by: EO 13144 (in part)' is reconciled: it is the same supersession, limited to Sections 1 through 7, and it leaves Section 8 in place.
scope_check: The inventory was corrected: fifteen clauses cover Sections 1 to 8, with the two-character span after Section 3(c) merged into Section 3(c). The ten pay schedules are attached tables (held only as blank page images in the Federal Register text layer) that Sections 1 to 5 make part of the order; they are treated as part of the clauses they are attached to and ended with them.
independent_command_check: Section 8 is an independent delegation; it does not depend on the schedules in Sections 1 to 7. Its continuing force rests on Executive Order 12748 section 2(c) as amended, which later orders (Executive Order 13415) left in place.
savings_check: Pay set under the 1999 schedules while Sections 1 to 6 were in force was paid and is an accrued effect; the supersession does not unwind it, and no held source says otherwise.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13111 (64 FR 2793, January 15, 1999) created a Task Force on Federal Training Technology (Sections 1 to 4) and an Advisory Committee on Expanding Training Opportunities (Sections 5 to 7), with definitions and a no-rights clause (Sections 8 and 9). Section 7(f) ended the Committee two years after the order; Executive Order 13188 moved that date to January 11, 2003; Executive Order 13218 rewrote Section 6; Executive Order 13316, effective September 30, 2003, revoked Sections 5 to 7 as part of a clean-up of committees that had terminated or whose work was completed. The held U.S. Code note prints the order with Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 still in text. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or sets an end for those sections, and the deadlines in them are not ends. The order is therefore claimed as in force on 2026-10-14 as to Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9, with Sections 5 to 7 ended with the Committee.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test for Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9: no own-terms end exists (the 18-month and six-month periods in Section 2 and the 30-day period in Section 1(b) are performance deadlines, not ends), and the only held later instruments that touch the order are Executive Orders 13188, 13218 and 13316, all of which concern the Advisory Committee in Sections 5 to 7. Executive Order 13316 revokes 'Sections 5 through 7' only.
Current basis: Current predicate: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 4103 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 as the order's text, marks Sections 5 to 7 as revoked, and shows no revocation of the rest; the bounded searches current-law:usc (1 hit, that note), current-law:ecfr (0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (6 hits, the amendments and the partial revocation) found no ending of Sections 1 to 4, 8 or 9.
savings_reason: Anything the Advisory Committee produced while it existed is an accrued effect of Sections 5 to 7; Executive Order 13316 revoked those sections and left Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 in place.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER": "The one candidate, Executive Order 13316's revocation of 'Sections 5 through 7', is accepted as the formal disposition of the fourteen Advisory Committee clauses; their first end is the Committee's own-terms end on 2003-01-11 (Section 7(f) as amended). Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 are not within that revocation, so the order stays YES."}
earlier_end_check: Sections 5 to 7 (the Advisory Committee): the Committee's own term ended on January 11, 2003 under Section 7(f) as amended by Executive Order 13188 (held text: the amendment replaces 'two years from the date of the order' with 'on January 11, 2003'). The order allows extension by the President before that date; no held instrument extends it (the number search of held texts, the Code note's complete amendment list of 13188, 13218 and 13316, and the later-events:ofr_catalog search show none), and Executive Order 13316 recites that the committees whose orders it revokes 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The cleanup revocation by Executive Order 13316 (effective September 30, 2003, section 6) is the formal disposition, not the first end. The absence of a held extension is a search result, not proof; if an extension exists the end would fall between January 11 and September 30, 2003. The record date is the stated termination day, January 11, 2003 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading would end the Committee as that day begins).
scope_check: Forty-nine machine-inventoried clauses cover Sections 1 to 9 and every lettered or numbered paragraph. Deadline clauses (Sections 1(b), 2(a) and 2(b)) are kept operative: a deadline is not an end, and no held source shows the designations, policy or options were performed, so the claim does not assert performance.
independent_command_check: Section 3 (agency duties) and Section 4 (OPM, Labor and Defense duties) command the named agencies independently of the Task Force's life; Section 8 definitions serve those sections. The Committee clauses depend on the Committee and ended with it.
savings_check: Advice given by the Committee before it ended is a historical fact, not a continuing command. No savings clause exists in the order's text for Sections 5 to 7.
